brief.summary_1line: Ravana encounters the ascetic Vedavati, who rejects him, curses his destruction, immolates herself, and is later reborn as Sita to bring about his downfall.

Vedavati leaps into a self-lit fire in the forest while flowers rain down from the sky.
Ravana, descending from his chariot in the Himalayan forest, confronts the radiant ascetic maiden Vedavati.

deep.rich_summary: This chapter recounts the origin story of Vedavati and its hidden link to Sita and Ravana’s eventual downfall. After receiving the divine sword Chandrahasa and extended life from Shiva, Ravana roams the world conquering kings. In the Himalayas he encounters Vedavati, a radiant ascetic princess performing severe penance to marry Vishnu, fulfilling her slain father’s wish. Ravana mocks her devotion and tries to seduce her, boasting of his own power. When she rebukes him and praises Vishnu, Ravana seizes her hair. In fury and defilement, Vedavati cuts off her hair, declares that she will be reborn to destroy him, and enters a sacred fire. The narrative reveals that she is later reborn as Janaka’s daughter—Sita—whose fate ultimately leads to Ravana’s destruction.

highlight_spans.why: Ravana receives Shiva’s brilliant sword Chandrahasa and an extended life, a pivotal moment empowering his later conquests.
Vedavati explains her divine vow: her father chose Vishnu as her destined husband, establishing the spiritual devotion that drives her penance.
Ravana’s lustful boasting and dismissal of Vishnu intensify the emotional and moral conflict between arrogance and devotion.
Vedavati cuts off her hair and vows rebirth for Ravana’s destruction—an iconic prophetic moment that foreshadows Sita’s role in the epic.
The revelation that Vedavati is reborn as Janaka’s daughter (Sita), linking this ascetic tragedy to the central narrative of the Ramayana.

top_scenes.scene_text: Ravana in his celestial chariot Pushpaka descending into a Himalayan forest and encountering the radiant ascetic Vedavati beneath tall pines.
Vedavati, blazing with fury, slicing off her seized hair as Ravana stands before her, the forest glowing with the fire she has kindled.
Vedavati stepping into the sacred fire as flowers rain from the heavens, divine light surrounding her as prophecy of her rebirth unfolds.
